titleEn: Hrīṃ is the Devī — the Mother's own seed, at the heart of the Navārṇa mantra.
meaningEn: Hrīṃ is the Devī's own seed — Bhuvaneśvarī, Mother of the worlds, and through her the Goddess in any form. The Tantras call it the māyā-bīja and read it letter by letter: ha is Śiva, ra is nature, ī is the Mother's māyā, and the hum ties them into one — Śiva and Śakti in a single breath. It stands at the centre of the Navārṇa, aiṃ hrīṃ klīṃ, and in the mantras of Bhuvaneśvarī and Lalitā.
meaningHi: ह्रीं देवी का अपना बीज है — भुवनेश्वरी, जगत की माँ, और उन्हीं से हर रूप में माँ। तंत्र इसे माया-बीज कहते हैं और अक्षर-अक्षर पढ़ते हैं: ह शिव, र प्रकृति, ई माँ की माया, और गूँज इन सबको एक कर देती है — शिव और शक्ति एक साँस में। नवार्ण मंत्र के बीच में यही है, ऐं ह्रीं क्लीं, और भुवनेश्वरी और ललिता के मंत्रों में भी।
sayItLike: hreem — 'h' + 'r' run together, long 'ee', then a hum

words.glossEn: prakṛti — nature, the stuff of the world
māyā — the Mother's power to appear as everything
words.glossHi: माया — माँ की वह ताक़त जिससे वह सब कुछ बनकर दिखती है

words.glossEn: the dot (ं) — the closing hum, bindu and nāda
words.glossHi: बिंदी (ं) — अंत की गूँज, बिन्दु और नाद
words.grammar: the kośa reads nāda as 'the mother of the world' and bindu as 'what takes sorrow away'

source.text: Varada Tantra as quoted in Woodroffe, Garland of Letters (1922); Śāradā-tilaka Tantra (11th c.), Bhuvaneśvarī paṭala
source.ref: the māyā-bīja; second seed of the Navārṇa, where the Saptaśatī vidhi names it 'hrīṃ śaktiḥ'
source.note: The letter-by-letter reading is the Tantras' kośa method — an attribution with authority inside those lineages, not etymology. A seed has no dictionary meaning.

significance.textSays: The Varada Tantra's kośa: ha is Śiva, ra is prakṛti, ī is Mahāmāyā, nāda the mother of the world, bindu the remover of sorrow. The Saptaśatī vidhi names hrīṃ the śakti of the Navārṇa.
significance.traditionSays: Bhuvaneśvarī's seed and the Devī's most-used single syllable; the middle of aiṃ hrīṃ klīṃ; present in the Pañcadaśī of Lalitā. Modern teachers read it as Mahālakṣmī within the Navārṇa.
significance.weDoNotClaim: Any effect from saying it. A seed has no dictionary meaning; tradition's reading is shown and the text named.
